messages:
sara: AcmeCorp reporting a big p99 regression on /v1/embeds after last night's infra push. They also saw intermittent 500s + auth token refresh errors. Hits started ~03:10 UTC. Attaching snippets from their traces and our sidecar logs.

sara: customer timeline: 03:05 normal, 03:10 sudden p99 ~4x, 03:12 started seeing 500s. They exercised embed route with 3 concurrent long-context requests.

sara: EXCERPT from sidecar log:
```
2026-03-17T03:11:08Z svc=embed node=eu-west-2-ax-12 host=/dev/nvme2n1 qdepth=256 latency_ms=1420 status=200 token_refresh=ok
2026-03-17T03:11:09Z svc=embed node=eu-west-2-ax-12 host=/dev/nvme2n1 qdepth=1024 latency_ms=5140 status=500 auth_err=token_refresh_failed
2026-03-17T03:11:10Z svc=embed node=eu-west-2-ax-12 host=/dev/nvme2n1 qdepth=900 latency_ms=4300 status=500 auth_err=token_cache_miss
```

mike: Which hosts are showing it? any pattern by zone or GPU type?

sara: Affected hosts: eu-west-2-ax-12, eu-west-2-ax-15. Both have NVIDIA driver 535.98 + microcode 0x3b applied last night (driver push #2026-03-16T22:00). Kernel is 6.2.15-rt. Not seeing same on older pools.

raj: Did we see KV cache thrash or a sudden spike in small IOs from token store?

sara: Token-store mediatype is local NVMe (partition nvme2n1p3). KV cache hitrate steady in metrics, but disk IO wait spiked. No memory OOMs.

kevin: I pulled iostat from eu-west-2-ax-12 at 03:11:
```
Device:         r/s     w/s     rkB/s    wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await
nvme2n1       1200.0  2100.0  153600.0  67200.0   112.0   78.4    12.5
```

kevin: avgqu-sz ~78 at spike time. That's much higher than baseline (~1-2).

leah: Customer repro (they sent steps): 3 parallel embedding requests with 30k tokens, synchronous client, token refresh header enabled. They say it started right after we flipped the new driver for eu-west-2.

incident-bot: alert: deploy "nvidia/535.98" rolled out to eu-west-2 at 2026-03-16T22:05:12Z by infra-cd.

mike: Thanks. Hypothesis: new driver/kernel interaction increased host io amplification for small sync workloads -> high NVMe queue depth -> increased latency -> auth token refresh requests time out -> 500s. Could be NVMe scheduling or new driver issuing more small reads.

raj: Agreed. Two immediate mitigations: 1) move traffic off affected nodes to fallback pool, 2) drain and repro on a drained node for deeper traces. Can we route customer to dedicated fallback?

sara: I requested fallback routing to dedicated-pool-3 for AcmeCorp, SRE accepted. Routing change applied at 03:25 UTC.

kevin: I'll cordon eu-west-2-ax-12 and restart nvme driver modules on ax-15 after snapshotting dmesg.

mike: Before we do kernel/driver restart, please capture `nvme list`, `nvme top`, `iostat -x 1 5`, `dmesg -T | tail -n 200`, and `perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep 30` on a repro node. Put artifacts in /tmp/incidents/1715002468.

kevin: Got artifacts. `dmesg` shows repeated `nvme: qpair timeout` lines and `NVME I/O 0x... delayed`. Vendor microcode messages referencing 0x3b.

leah: After routing, customer reported latencies returned to baseline within ~3 minutes and 500s stopped. Confirming recovery.

sara: Customer happy with fallback but asked for ETA on fix and assurance it won't recur. They're on a heavy SLA.

mike: Short-term plan: keep rollback/routing in place for AcmeCorp until we have reproducer and vendor confirmation. Medium: reproduce in staging with same driver+kernel, trace NVMe scheduling. Long-term: add synthetic qdepth test to our canary that simulates small synchronous embed bursts.

raj: Assigning postmortem owner: raj. Action items I'm adding:
- reproduce in staging with driver 535.98 + kernel 6.2.15-rt (owner: raj)
- open vendor bug with NVIDIA and OEM for NVMe microcode interaction (owner: mike)
- add runbook steps for draining + fallback routing (owner: kevin)
- add synthetic embed stress test to CI (owner: eng-dex)

kevin: I'll also add a short-term mitigator to the autoscaler: lower max_concurrency per-host for embed service in eu-west-2 to reduce sync I/O bursts.

leah: Note for support: if customer sees token_refresh failures, route to fallback pool and file incident.

mike: We should also verify our token refresh client has sane timeouts and exponential backoff; small I/O blips shouldn't cascade to 500s. (Follow-up: open a small PR to add jitter/backoff, owner: sara).

sara: I'll draft a customer-facing summary and ETA later today.

raj: Quick notes from initial triage: root cause likely interaction between host kernel IO scheduler + NVIDIA driver 535.98 microcode path that increases queue depth under sync workloads causing token refresh clients to hit latency/timeouts. Not 100% until vendor response and regression repro.

mike: Marking incident as mitigated since customer routed and baseline restored. Keeping thread open for follow-ups and postmortem.

leah: Thanks all. I'll update the support ticket and loop customer in. :white_check_mark:
